records.claim: The Monell resolution created a precedent that for the first time established local government monetary accountability for unconstitutional acts and created the right to obtain damages from municipalities in such cases.

records.claim: The accountability established in Monell is a legal doctrine known as Monell liability, which has been further developed by subsequent case law.
records.quote: This accountability is a legal doctrine known as Monell liability that has been further developed by subsequent case law.

records.claim: Under the Monell holding, municipal entities can be sued under §1983 only pursuant to a policy or custom, which is distinct from liability of individual defendants under §1983.
records.quote: The Court's holding means that liability for an individual defendant sued under §1983, who can be liable for any constitutional violation (absent immunities), even if the conduct is unauthorized or a one-off incident, is distinct from liability for municipal entities, who can be sued under §1983 only pursuant to a policy or custom.

records.claim: Municipal liability under Monell can arise from either an affirmative policy or custom or a policy by omission.
records.quote: This can mean either an affirmative policy or custom or a policy by omission.

records.claim: In Pembaur v. City of Cincinnati, the Court held that a single decision made by a municipal policy maker can establish policy sufficient for Monell liability.
records.quote: In Pembaur v. City of Cincinnati , the Court held that a single decision made by municipal policy maker can establish policy sufficient for Monell liability.

records.claim: In City of St. Louis v. Praprotnik (1988), the Court held that officials with final policy-making authority and responsibilities under state law for making policy in that area of a city's business are municipal policy-makers.
records.quote: In determining who is a municipal policy maker in City of St. Louis v. Praprotnik (1988), the Court held that officials with final policy-making authority and responsibilities under state law for making policy in that area of city's business, are municipal policy-makers.

records.claim: In City of Canton v. Harris, the Court held that a municipality can be liable for a failure to train its employees when this failure constitutes deliberate indifference to the person whose rights were violated.
records.quote: Regarding policies of omission, the Court held in City of Canton v. Harris that a municipality can be liable for a failure to train its employees when this failure constitutes a deliberate indifference to the person whose rights were violated.

records.claim: The same standard of deliberate indifference applies to a municipality's failure to screen employees.
records.quote: The same standard of deliberate indifference applies to failure to screen employees.

records.claim: The City stated that it approved of the Court of Appeals' analysis on §1983 liability and that any other result would render virtually meaningless the Court's decision in Monroe v. Pape.

records.claim: Physical change alters only the form, size, or state of a substance without forming a new substance, whereas chemical change produces one or more new substances with different properties.

records.claim: A physical change is a change in shape, size, or state in which the composition of the substance remains the same, and it is usually reversible by simple physical processes.
records.quote: Physical change: A change in shape, size, or state in which the composition of the substance remains the same. Usually reversible by simple physical processes.

records.claim: A chemical change (chemical reaction) is a change in which one or more new substances are formed with properties different from the original substances, and it is often difficult to reverse by simple physical means.
records.quote: Chemical change (chemical reaction): A change in which one or more new substances are formed with properties different from the original substances. Often difficult to reverse by simple physical means.

records.claim: In a chemical change, atoms rearrange and new bonds form while old bonds break, creating new substances, and energy is absorbed or released due to these bond changes.
records.quote: Chemical change: Atoms rearrange and new bonds form while old bonds break, creating new substances. Energy is absorbed or released due to bond changes.

records.claim: In a physical change, particles of the substance remain the same and only their arrangement, spacing, or motion changes, such as when a solid turns to a liquid.
records.quote: Physical change: Particles of the substance remain the same; only their arrangement, spacing, or motion changes (e.g., solid to liquid).

records.claim: Bubbles forming without heating or boiling usually indicate a chemical change.
records.quote: Gas evolution: Bubbles without heating/boiling usually indicate a chemical change.

records.claim: The formation of a solid in a solution (precipitate) shows a chemical change.
records.quote: Precipitate formation: A solid forming in a solution shows a chemical change.

records.claim: Colour change, irreversibility, or gas formation alone are not perfect tests of a chemical change, since boiling water makes steam (a gas) but is a physical change.
records.quote: Caution: Colour change, irreversibility, or gas formation alone are not perfect tests. For example, boiling water makes steam (gas) but is a physical change.

records.claim: Dissolving salt or sugar in water is a physical change in which no new substance is formed, and the solute can be recovered by evaporation or crystallization.
records.quote: Dissolving salt or sugar in water: Physical change; no new substance; solute can be recovered by evaporation/crystallization.

records.claim: Rusting of iron is a chemical change in which iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form rust (iron oxides) with different properties.
records.quote: Rusting of iron: Chemical change; iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form rust (iron oxides) with different properties.

records.quote: Burning a candle: Both changes occur. Melting of wax near the flame is physical; burning of wax (forming carbon dioxide and water) and burning of wick are chemical.

records.claim: Melting ice, freezing water, and boiling water are physical changes in which the state changes but the water remains water.
records.quote: Melting ice, freezing water, boiling water: Physical change; state changes but water remains water.

records.claim: A costing system is a framework used by firms to estimate the cost of their products for profitability analysis, inventory valuation and cost control.

records.claim: The goal of a costing system is to identify the amount spent by a company to produce a product or provide a service.

records.claim: Job order costing is used when products are made based on specific customer orders, with each job accounted for separately and direct materials, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead tracked for each job.

records.claim: Job order costing is often used in industries like construction, shipbuilding, or custom furniture.

records.claim: Process costing is used when a company produces a large volume of identical products, with costs accumulated for a process or department and the average cost per unit calculated.

records.claim: Process costing is often used in industries like oil refining, food production, or chemical manufacturing.

records.claim: Activity-based costing assigns costs to products based on the activities used in their production, allocating each activity's cost to each product to the extent the product uses that activity.

records.claim: Activity-based costing can be more accurate than traditional costing systems, especially for complex, modern manufacturing processes.
records.quote: This system can be more accurate than traditional costing systems, especially for complex, modern manufacturing processes.

records.claim: Standard costing uses estimates or standards to assign costs to products, and the company compares actual costs with standard costs to measure performance.

records.claim: In the furniture example, the costs of the custom dining table job are accumulated in a job cost sheet and the total cost is used to determine its price.

records.claim: Non-porous rocks cannot store water, so the peak discharge of a river increases as more water enters the river rather than being stored in the drainage basin.

records.claim: The molar heat capacity of a chemical substance is the amount of energy that must be added, in the form of heat, to one mole of the substance in order to cause an increase of one unit in its temperature.
records.quote: The molar heat capacity of a chemical substance is the amount of energy that must be added, in the form of heat , to one mole of the substance in order to cause an increase of one unit in its temperature .

records.claim: The SI unit of molar heat capacity is joule per kelvin per mole (J⋅K−1⋅mol−1).
records.quote: The SI unit of molar heat capacity is joule per kelvin per mole , J⋅K −1 ⋅mol −1 .

records.claim: At atmospheric pressure, the isobaric molar heat capacity of water just above the melting point is about 76 J⋅K−1⋅mol−1, while that of ice just below that point is about 37.84 J⋅K−1⋅mol−1.
records.quote: For example, at atmospheric pressure , the (isobaric) molar heat capacity of water just above the melting point is about 76 J⋅K −1 ⋅mol −1 , but that of ice just below that point is about 37.84 J⋅K −1 ⋅mol −1 .

records.claim: While a substance is undergoing a phase transition, such as melting or boiling, its molar heat capacity is technically infinite, because the heat goes into changing its state rather than raising its temperature.
records.quote: While the substance is undergoing a phase transition , such as melting or boiling, its molar heat capacity is technically infinite , because the heat goes into changing its state rather than raising its temperature.

records.claim: The molar heat capacity generally increases with the molar mass, often varies with temperature and pressure, and is different for each state of matter.
records.quote: The molar heat capacity generally increases with the molar mass, often varies with temperature and pressure, and is different for each state of matter .

records.claim: The measured molar heat capacity of a substance, especially a gas, may be significantly higher when heated at constant pressure (isobaric) than when heated at constant volume (isochoric).
records.quote: Like specific heat, the measured molar heat capacity of a substance, especially a gas, may be significantly higher when the sample is allowed to expand as it is heated ( at constant pressure , or isobaric ) than when it is heated in a closed vessel that prevents expansion ( at constant volume , or isochoric ).

records.claim: The ratio between the molar heat capacities at constant pressure and constant volume is the same heat capacity ratio obtained from the corresponding specific heat capacities.
records.quote: The ratio between the two, however, is the same heat capacity ratio obtained from the corresponding specific heat capacities.

records.claim: The concept of molar heat capacity is not appropriate for substances whose precise composition is not known, or whose molar mass is not well defined, such as polymers and oligomers of indeterminate molecular size.
records.quote: The concept is not appropriate for substances whose precise composition is not known, or whose molar mass is not well defined, such as polymers and oligomers of indeterminate molecular size.

records.claim: The atom-molar heat capacity is the heat capacity of a sample divided by the number of moles of atoms instead of moles of molecules.

records.claim: An alluvial fan is an accumulation of sediments that fans out from a concentrated source of sediments, such as a narrow canyon emerging from an escarpment.
records.quote: An alluvial fan is an accumulation of sediments that fans out from a concentrated source of sediments, such as a narrow canyon emerging from an escarpment .

records.quote: This accumulation is shaped like a section of a shallow cone , [ 1 ] with its apex at the source of sediments.

records.claim: Some giant alluvial fans have areas of almost 20,000 square kilometres.
records.quote: Some giant alluvial fans have areas of almost 20,000 square kilometres (7,700 sq mi) .

records.claim: The slope of an alluvial fan measured from the apex is generally concave, with the steepest slope near the apex (the proximal fan or fanhead) and becoming less steep further out (the medial fan or midfan) and shallowing at the edges (the distal fan or outer fan).
records.quote: The slope measured from the apex is generally concave, with the steepest slope near the apex (the proximal fan [ 4 ] or fanhead [ 5 ] ) and becoming less steep further out (the medial fan or midfan ) and shallowing at the edges of the fan (the distal fan or outer fan ).

records.claim: Sieve deposits, which are lobes of coarse gravel, may be present on the proximal fan.
records.quote: Sieve deposits , which are lobes of coarse gravel, may be present on the proximal fan.

records.claim: The sediments in an alluvial fan are usually coarse and poorly sorted, with the coarsest sediments found on the proximal fan.
records.quote: The sediments in an alluvial fan are usually coarse and poorly sorted, with the coarsest sediments found on the proximal fan.

records.claim: When there is enough space in the alluvial plain for sediment deposits to fan out without contacting other valley walls or rivers, an unconfined alluvial fan develops.
records.quote: When there is enough space in the alluvial plain for all of the sediment deposits to fan out without contacting other valley walls or rivers, an unconfined alluvial fan develops.

records.claim: When the alluvial plain is more restricted and the fan contacts topographic barriers, a confined fan is formed.
records.quote: When the alluvial plain is more restricted, so that the fan comes into contact with topographic barriers, a confined fan is formed.

records.claim: Wave or channel erosion of the fan edge (lateral erosion) sometimes produces a "toe-trimmed" fan, in which the edge is marked by a small escarpment.
records.quote: Wave or channel erosion of the edge of the fan ( lateral erosion ) sometimes produces a "toe-trimmed" fan, in which the edge of the fan is marked by a small escarpment.

records.claim: On average, people are just as genetically related to their parents as they are to their siblings.
records.quote: On average, we are just as related to our parents as we are to our siblings--but there can be some slight differences!

records.quote: We share 1/2 of our genetic material with our mother and 1/2 with our father. We also share 1/2 of our DNA, on average, with our brothers and sisters.

records.claim: Genetic likeness drops by half with each increasingly distant branch in the family tree.
records.quote: Our genetic likeness continues to drop by 1/2 with each increasingly distant branch in the family tree.

records.claim: Everyone shares exactly 50% of their DNA with each parent, while people share on average 50% of their DNA with their siblings.
records.quote: while everyone shares exactly 50% of their DNA with each parent, we share on average 50% of our DNA with our siblings.

records.claim: A person can be slightly more or less than 50% related to a sibling.
records.quote: You can actually be slightly more or less than 50% related to a sibling, for reasons that are explained below.

records.claim: Human DNA is coiled into 23 pairs of chromosomes, giving 46 chromosomes in total.

records.claim: Egg cells and sperm contain only a single copy of each of the 23 chromosomes, one half of each pair.

records.claim: Recombination swaps DNA between the matching chromosomes in each pair before the pairs are split in eggs and sperm.
records.quote: Recombination swaps DNA around between the matching chromosomes in each pair.

records.claim: During reproduction, the egg's 23 chromosomes and the sperm's 23 chromosomes combine, so a baby has 46 chromosomes and shares exactly half its genes with each parent.
records.quote: During reproduction, the 23 chromosomes in the mother's egg and the 23 chromosomes in the father's sperm combine. This results in a baby with an entire set of 46 chromosomes who shares exactly half its genes with its mother and half its genes with its father!

records.claim: People are usually 50% genetically related to their sisters and brothers.

records.quote: A fan may provoke an asthma attack when airborne allergens are inhaled, triggering bronchial spasms and constriction (narrowing).

records.claim: A fan can worsen dry eyes (keratoconjunctivitis sicca) by accelerating tear evaporation.
records.quote: A fan can worsen dry eyes ( keratoconjunctivitis sicca ) by accelerating tear evaporation.

records.claim: In older adults, infants, and people with heart disease, a fan should not be used as the sole source of cooling when temperatures are over 95 F.
records.quote: In older adults, infants, and people with heart disease, a fan should not be used as the sole source of cooling when temperatures are over 95 F.

records.claim: Using a fan as the sole source of cooling in these conditions may fail to reduce core body temperature and lead to potentially life-threatening heat strain.
records.quote: Doing so may fail to reduce the core body temperature and lead to potentially life-threatening heat strain.

records.claim: A fan may contribute to sinus infection, especially when the airflow is dry, cold, or directed toward the face.
records.quote: A fan may contribute to sinus infection , especially when the airflow is dry, cold, or directed toward the face.

records.claim: Dry air can dehydrate the nasal lining and thicken mucus, leading to congestion and creating a hotbed for bacterial growth.
records.quote: Dry air can dehydrate the nasal lining and thicken mucus, leading to congestion and creating a hotbed for bacterial growth.

records.claim: Running the fan for one to three hours may give enough cooling without drying the nose or eyes.
records.quote: Running the fan for one to three hours may give you enough cooling without drying your nose or eyes out.

records.claim: Air circulation can reduce the risk of mold in damp rooms.
records.quote: Air circulation can reduce the risk of mold in damp rooms.

records.claim: Lower humidity may also make bedrooms less favorable for dust mites.
records.quote: Lower humidity may also make bedrooms less favorable for dust mites .

records.claim: Rama rejected Shurpanakha's advances, telling her that he was faithful to his wife Sita and would never take another wife.
records.quote: Rama rejected her advances, telling her that he was faithful to his wife Sita and thus would never take another wife.

records.claim: Sita was raised by King Janaka of Mithila as his own daughter, married Rama of Ayodhya, and accompanied him on his exile.
records.quote: Sita was raised by King Janaka of Mithila as his own daughter. She married Rama of Ayodhya and accompanied him on his exile.

records.claim: Sita is regarded as an avatar of the goddess of prosperity, Lakshmi.
records.quote: She is famed for her virtue and beauty and is regarded as an avatar of the goddess of prosperity, Lakshmi .

records.claim: Subahu was killed by Rama.
records.quote: Subahu was killed by Rama.

records.claim: Sugriva was a vanara and the younger brother of Vali, whom he succeeded as ruler of the kingdom of Kishkindha.
records.quote: Sugriva : A vanara. He was the younger brother of Vali , whom he succeeded as ruler of the vanara the kingdom of Kishkindha .

records.claim: Sugriva was the spiritual son of Surya.
records.quote: He was the spiritual son of Surya .

records.claim: Sugriva aided Rama in his quest to liberate Sita from captivity at the hands of Ravana.
records.quote: Sugriva aided Rama in his quest to liberate his wife Sita from the captivity at the hands of Ravana.

records.claim: Suketu was a yaksha who performed a yajna to get an heir and after the ritual got a daughter named Tataka.
records.quote: Suketu: A yaksha who performed a yajna to get an heir, with the strength equal to thousand elephants. After the ritual, he got a daughter named Tataka .

records.claim: Sumali was married to Ketumati, with whom he had ten sons and four daughters.
records.quote: Sumali was married to Ketumati with whom he had ten sons ( Prahasta , Akampana , Vikata, Kalikamukha, Dhumraksha, Danda, Suprasva, Sanhradi, Praghasa, and Bhaskarna) and four daughters (Raka, Pushpotkata, Kaikasi, Kumbhinasi).

records.claim: Kaikasi, a daughter of Sumali, was married to sage Vishrava, who later gave birth to Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Vibhishana, and Shurpanakha.
records.quote: One of his daughters Kaikasi was married to sage Vishrava who later gave birth to Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Vibhishana, and Shurpanakha.

records.claim: Sumitra was the second wife of King Dasharatha of Ayodhya and the mother of the twins Lakshmana and Shatrughna.
records.quote: Sumitra : The second wife of King Dasharatha of Ayodhya. She was the mother of the twins Lakshmana and Shatrughna.

records.claim: Sunayana was the queen of Mithila, wife of King Janaka, and the mother of Sita and Urmila.
records.quote: Sunayana : The queen of Mithila, wife of King Janaka, and the mother of Sita and Urmila.
